# dokploy_web_server_settings (Resource)

The settings of the Dokploy host: the dashboard domain, the server IP, the Docker and access-log cleanup, and the number of concurrent builds. Use `dokploy_server` for a remote server.

~> Each Dokploy installation has one settings record. Declare this resource once. `terraform destroy` removes the resource from the state only: the server keeps the current values. Dokploy Cloud has no web server settings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Serve the Dokploy dashboard on a domain with a Let's Encrypt certificate,
# and allow two builds at the same time on the Dokploy host. Declare this
# resource once for each Dokploy installation.
resource "dokploy_web_server_settings" "this" {
  host               = "dokploy.example.com"
  https              = true
  certificate_type   = "letsencrypt"
  lets_encrypt_email = "ops@example.com"

  builds_concurrency = 2
  log_cleanup_cron   = "0 3 * * *"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `builds_concurrency` (Number) Number of builds that run at the same time on the Dokploy host, from 1 to 100. Defaults to `1`.
- `certificate_type` (String) Certificate of the dashboard domain: `letsencrypt`, `custom`, or `none`. Defaults to `none`.
- `enable_docker_cleanup` (Boolean) Remove unused Docker images, containers, and build cache on the Dokploy host every day. Defaults to `true`.
- `host` (String) Domain of the Dokploy dashboard, for example `dokploy.example.com`. A change rewrites the Traefik route of the dashboard. Omit it to serve the dashboard on the IP only.
- `https` (Boolean) Serve the dashboard domain over HTTPS. Defaults to `false`.
- `lets_encrypt_email` (String) Email address for the Let's Encrypt account of the dashboard certificate.
- `log_cleanup_cron` (String) Cron expression of the Traefik access-log cleanup, which keeps the last 1000 lines. Defaults to `0 0 * * *`. Set `""` to stop the cleanup. Dokploy does not validate the expression.
- `server_ip` (String) Public IP of the Dokploy host. Dokploy uses it for the generated `traefik.me` domains. If you omit it, the server keeps the IP that the installer detected.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Id of the settings record.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = dokploy_web_server_settings.this
  id = "63e946a9-516d-47fb-b863-32bf308592c6"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is the id of the settings record. Read it from the Dokploy API with
# settings.getWebServerSettings.
terraform import dokploy_web_server_settings.this 63e946a9-516d-47fb-b863-32bf308592c6
```
